chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Umar ibn Hanzalah said:
I carried the ribitha in a small bag until I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him about it, so he said, 'Eat it,' and he said, 'It has a peel.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', who said: I wrote to him, 'People differ regarding the ribitha, so what do you see regarding it?' He wrote back (peace be upon him), 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الرَّبِيثَا: Ribitha, a type of dried or preserved fish
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهَا: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is ribitha (dried fish) permissible to eat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling on *ribitha* (dried fish), with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permitting its consumption including the skin, thereby resolving juristic differences through direct textual evidence. The inclusion of both oral instruction and written reply highlights the scholarly method of addressing specific fiqh queries during the era of the Imams, emphasizing the permissibility of preserved marine foods as a practical provision for the community.
